findings.title: Anonymous visitors get every permission (write/upload/zip) in the public folder; settings.guestPermissions is never consulted
findings.evidence: `return { space, root: paths.publicDir, perms: new Set(PERMISSIONS) }` -- guestPermissions is never read. An unauthenticated client gets a session + CSRF token from GET /api/session, then POST /api/delete {space:'public',items:['/report.pdf']} passes need(...,'write'). PUT /api/content, /api/move, /api/rename, /api/upload and /api/unzip on public files are open to any visitor.

findings.title: Rename route checks only 'read' instead of 'write'
findings.evidence: `const a = need({ user, ip }, body.space, 'read')` in POST /api/rename, followed by `moveSync(from, to)`. A user whose publicPermissions are only ['read'] sends POST /api/rename {space:'public',path:'/manual.pdf',name:'x.pdf'} and renames files in the public folder.

findings.title: Download route checks 'read' instead of 'download'
findings.evidence: `const a = need({ user, ip }, query.space, 'read')` in GET /api/download, then `return fileResponse(abs, ...)`. A user granted only 'read' sends GET /api/download?space=public&path=/secret.pdf and gets the file although download was withheld; GET /api/content requires 'read','download'.

findings.title: Client IP is taken from the first (client-controlled) X-Forwarded-For entry
findings.evidence: `return request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',').at(0)?.trim() || socketIp` -- with TRUST_PROXY=true the proxy appends the real IP last. An attacker sends POST /api/login with a new X-Forwarded-For each attempt, getting a fresh lockout key every time and spoofing audit-log IPs.

findings.title: Login lockout key is case-sensitive while user lookup is case-insensitive
findings.evidence: `const key = `${ip}|${username}`` -- but findUser compares lowercased names. After failures for 'admin', the attacker tries 'Admin', 'aDmin', 'ADMIN', ... each a fresh lockout bucket for the same account.

findings.title: Signed-in sessions effectively never expire on access (TTL multiplied by 1000 and measured from creation)
findings.evidence: `if (Date.now() - s.created > ttlOf(s) * 1000)` -- ttlOf already returns milliseconds, so 168 h becomes about 19 years. A stolen fc_sid stays valid as long as it is used before the hourly purgeExpiredSessions idle sweep.

findings.title: Update package files are checked only by size; the manifest SHA-256 is never verified
findings.evidence: `if (statSync(abs).size !== want?.size || false) throw bad(...)` -- no hash is computed for any listed file although the README promises SHA-256 checks. A same-size tampered server.js passes POST /api/admin/update/stage and /apply. Needs an admin to upload it.

findings.title: Staging runs the uploaded package's code (smoke test) before the password step-up, with its scratch data inside DATA_DIR
findings.evidence: `const staged = await stagePackage(done.path, done.size)` in POST /api/admin/update/stage calls only requireAdmin, no confirmPassword. stagePackage -> smokeTest runs `Bun.spawn([process.execPath, join(dir, SERVER_FILE)]...)` with scratch under paths.app inside DATA_DIR. Someone holding a stolen admin cookie uploads a package and POSTs /stage; their server.js runs on the host as the app user and can read ../../users.json and sessions.json, although the comments say a stolen cookie is not enough to install code.
